title: Stella Parton slams AI posts and snarky tweets flooding social media after Dolly Parton's death
description: Dolly Parton's sister Stella has spoken out against the wave of AI-generated posts and insensitive social media commentary targeting her family in the days following the country icon's death at age 80.

title: Dolly Parton's Sister Stella Slams AI Posts and Snarky Tweets Flooding Social Media After Country Icon's Death
description: Stella Parton has spoken out about the artificial intelligence generated content and dismissive online commentary that has overwhelmed her family since the death of country legend Dolly Parton at age 80. In a heartfelt Instagram letter, the 77 year old singer-songwriter urged fans to show compassion and use her sister's life as an example of tolerance, while reflecting on Dolly's secret cancer battle and her plans for a new Nashville hotel and museum.

title: Brookhaven Lab to lead $11.5M AI project aimed at strengthening nation’s electric grid
description: By Charlie Zeeve Brookhaven National Laboratory has been selected to lead an $11.5 million U.S. Department of Energy project that will use artificial intelligence to help utilities better plan and operate the nation’s increasingly complex electric grid. The project, known as Foundation Models for the Electric Grid, or Grid FM 2.0, was announced Tuesday at Brookhaven Lab as part of the DOE’s Genesis Mission. The initiative brings together national laboratories, universities, utilities, government agencies and technology companies to develop AI tools capable of examining vastly more potential grid conditions than current methods allow. DOE Assistant Secretary for the Office of Electricity Catherine Jereza said the project aims to develop the capability to evaluate as many as 1 billion potential grid scenarios in 24 hours. “Twenty-three years ago, the lights went out because we couldn’t see far enough ahead,” Jereza said, referring to the 2003 Northeast blackout. “Today, thanks to Grid FM 2.0 and the Genesis mission, we’re building a grid that can see a billion possibilities in a single day.” The technology could help utilities make faster decisions about connecting new businesses and large energy users, including data centers and advanced manufacturing facilities, while identifying ways to meet growing electricity demand without unnecessary infrastructure costs. Brookhaven Lab Director John Hill said the project represents an opportunity to move AI research into real-world applications. “The grid is arguably the most important critical infrastructure our nation has,” Hill said, noting that it includes 200 million access points, 50 million transformers, 10 million energy sources and 7 million miles of wires. Electricity demand is growing as AI, advanced manufacturing and other emerging industries expand, while connecting new sources of generation and major new users to the grid can be a lengthy process, Hill said. Brookhaven is leading the project with 26 collaborators, spanning national laboratories, universities, government, utilities and the private sector. The broader Grid FM community includes more than 150 organizations. Local energy organizations participating include the Long Island Power Authority and New York Power Authority, while other partners include New York ISO, National Grid and Con Edison. Technology partners include IBM, GE, NVIDIA, Microsoft and others. Hendrik Hamann, Brookhaven’s chief AI scientist for Innovation, Science and Security and the project’s principal investigator, said the goal is not simply to generate billions of possible answers, but to use those possibilities to arrive at better decisions. “The goal is to create a single better decision out of all these billions of answers that we will be getting,” Hamann said. The project will also move toward real-world utility demonstrations, with plans for at least two deployments. Brookhaven researchers will work on applications involving grid resiliency, interconnection and expansion planning. The Phase II award builds on Brookhaven’s broader participation in the Genesis Mission. DOE previously awarded the lab seven Phase I projects, while Brookhaven researchers are contributing to 29 additional Phase I projects led by other organizations. Hill said the latest award marks an important milestone, but also the beginning of significant work. “We’re excited about what comes next and what this team can accomplish for DOE and for the nation,” he said.
